There's a reason all monopolies fail in the long run. Its not that some people working within the monopolies don't want them to change. Very often people on the inside see the writing on the wall and they themselves are the actual innovators. However, the business itself compels those innovations be stifled. Magnetic tape recording was invented in the 1930s at Bell Laboratories. When the engineering team showed it off, the senior management of Ma Bell told them to shelf the project because, "if people are able to record their telephone calls, they wont have as much need for our phone service..."

In 1979 an engineer at Sony looking through old patents saw it and that the patent had expired. He showed his bosses how they could save music on magnetic tapes, which eventually led to the Walkman, and ironically, answering machines.

The bell executive wasn't acting outrageously. However, his job required that the established business model not be endangered. Rather than seeing magnetic recording for all the businesses it could become, he could only see it as a threat and now Ma Bell no longer exists. Sadly, that mentality is the standard in executive suites, rather than the exception.
